+# The deploy hook
+
+By the time the deploy hook is called, the post and its revision are
+already committed — see [publishing a post](./publish.md). Rolling that
+back because a webhook timed out would throw away real work over a problem
+that's usually transient and, worse, outside this app's control entirely.
+Instead, the call reports back `{ ok: boolean }`, and the publish response
+passes that along as `deployTriggered`.
+
+## Retry policy
+
+Three attempts, with a linear backoff between them. That's tuned for a
+cold serverless function taking a moment to wake up, not for a target
+that's genuinely down: three attempts a few hundred milliseconds apart
+won't save a publish from a deploy hook that's been deleted or
+misconfigured.
+
+When every attempt fails, the failure is logged at `error` and the call
+returns `{ ok: false }` rather than throwing, so the publish route always
+gets a definite answer either way.

+---
+type: Specification
+title: Publishing a post
+description: The three-step write a publish performs and what a caller observes when the deploy hook doesn't fire.
+---
+
+# Publishing a post
+
+Publishing a post does three things, in order:
+
+1. Write a `revisions` row — a snapshot of the post's title and body at the
+   moment of publish.
+2. Flip the post's `status` to `published`.
+3. Call the site's deploy hook.
+
+The first two happen as one transaction: either both happen or neither does.
+The third is best-effort — see [the deploy hook](./deploy-hook.md) for the
+retry policy and why its failure doesn't roll back the first two steps.
+
+## What a caller sees
+
+The publish response carries `deployTriggered: boolean`. The editor tells
+the author which case they're in rather than treating publish as either
+fully succeeded or fully failed:
+
+- `deployTriggered: true` — "Published. The site will rebuild shortly."
+- `deployTriggered: false` — "Published, but the deploy didn't fire — you
+  may need to trigger it yourself." See
+  [recovering a missed build](../guides/desk.md#missed-build).
+
+A draft save (a title/body edit without publishing) never writes a
+revision; see [revisions](./revisions.md).
+
+## Undoing a publish
+
+There's no unpublish action. A revision records what went out; it isn't an
+undo mechanism. Reverting live content means editing the post back to a
+previous revision's text and publishing again.

+
+# Revisions
+
+A post becomes published together with the revision snapshot written for it
+in the same transaction. A failed deploy hook leaves both the published
+post and its revision in place — see
+[publishing a post](./publish.md).
+

+
+The Revisions screen groups snapshots by post. Each group's heading uses
+the post's *current* title; each snapshot card uses the title that was
+saved *at that publish*. Within a post, snapshots are newest first.
+
+A draft save updates the post without adding a snapshot: only a publish
+writes a revision.

+
+Publishing a post does three things, in order:

+   moment of publish.
+2. Flip the post's `status` to `published`.
+3. Call the site's deploy hook.

+The third is best-effort — see [the deploy hook](./deploy-hook.md) for the
+retry policy and why its failure doesn't roll back the first two steps.

+the author which case they're in rather than treating publish as either
+fully succeeded or fully failed:

+  may need to trigger it yourself." See

+
+A draft save (a title/body edit without publishing) never writes a
+revision; see [revisions](./revisions.md).
+
+## Undoing a publish
+
+There's no unpublish action. A revision records what went out; it isn't an
+undo mechanism. Reverting live content means editing the post back to a
+previous revision's text and publishing again.

+
+# The deploy hook
+
+By the time the deploy hook is called, the post and its revision are
+already committed — see [publishing a post](./publish.md). Rolling that
+back because a webhook timed out would throw away real work over a problem
+that's usually transient and, worse, outside this app's control entirely.
+Instead, the call reports back `{ ok: boolean }`, and the publish response
+passes that along as `deployTriggered`.
+
+## Retry policy
+
+Three attempts, with a linear backoff between them. That's tuned for a
+cold serverless function taking a moment to wake up, not for a target
+that's genuinely down: three attempts a few hundred milliseconds apart
+won't save a publish from a deploy hook that's been deleted or
+misconfigured.
+
+When every attempt fails, the failure is logged at `error` and the call
+returns `{ ok: false }` rather than throwing, so the publish route always
+gets a definite answer either way.

+---

+description: The three-step write a publish performs and what a caller observes when the deploy hook doesn't fire.
+---
+
+# Publishing a post
+
+Publishing a post does three things, in order:
+
+1. Write a `revisions` row — a snapshot of the post's title and body at the
+   moment of publish.
+2. Flip the post's `status` to `published`.
+3. Call the site's deploy hook.
+
+The first two happen as one transaction: either both happen or neither does.
+The third is best-effort — see [the deploy hook](./deploy-hook.md) for the
+retry policy and why its failure doesn't roll back the first two steps.
+
+## What a caller sees
+
+The publish response carries `deployTriggered: boolean`. The editor tells
+the author which case they're in rather than treating publish as either
+fully succeeded or fully failed:
+
+- `deployTriggered: true` — "Published. The site will rebuild shortly."
+- `deployTriggered: false` — "Published, but the deploy didn't fire — you
+  may need to trigger it yourself." See
+  [recovering a missed build](../guides/desk.md#missed-build).
+
+A draft save (a title/body edit without publishing) never writes a
+revision; see [revisions](./revisions.md).
+
+## Undoing a publish
+
+There's no unpublish action. A revision records what went out; it isn't an
+undo mechanism. Reverting live content means editing the post back to a
+previous revision's text and publishing again.

+cold serverless function taking a moment to wake up, not for a target

+# Publishing a post
+
+Publishing a post does three things, in order:
+
+1. Write a `revisions` row — a snapshot of the post's title and body at the
+   moment of publish.
+2. Flip the post's `status` to `published`.
+3. Call the site's deploy hook.
+
+The first two happen as one transaction: either both happen or neither does.
+The third is best-effort — see [the deploy hook](./deploy-hook.md) for the
+retry policy and why its failure doesn't roll back the first two steps.
+
+## What a caller sees
+
+The publish response carries `deployTriggered: boolean`. The editor tells
+the author which case they're in rather than treating publish as either
+fully succeeded or fully failed:
+
+- `deployTriggered: true` — "Published. The site will rebuild shortly."
+- `deployTriggered: false` — "Published, but the deploy didn't fire — you
+  may need to trigger it yourself." See
+  [recovering a missed build](../guides/desk.md#missed-build).
+
+A draft save (a title/body edit without publishing) never writes a
+revision; see [revisions](./revisions.md).
+

+
+There's no unpublish action. A revision records what went out; it isn't an
+undo mechanism. Reverting live content means editing the post back to a
+previous revision's text and publishing again.
